title: Data and code for: Advice from multiple AI models reduces overreliance only when their errors diverge
description: The paper studies overreliance on AI. It asks whether advice from three AI models built by different developers, rather than one, reduces how often people adopt a wrong AI answer, and whether this depends on the models making the same errors. Seeing three models reduced the adoption of wrong answers, but only when the models' errors diverged. A wrong answer repeated by a second model was adopted as often as a single model's wrong answer. This archive holds the analysis code, study materials, aggregate data and a simulated dataset for Studies 1–2 (N = 441) of 'Advice from multiple AI models reduces overreliance only when their errors diverge'. Individual-level data are not included: under the consent participants gave, they cannot be shared publicly but are available to qualified researchers on request. Code is released under the MIT License; data, materials and documentation under CC BY 4.0, except MMLU-Pro content (Apache 2.0).
